entities.name: MLN8054
observations: Selective AURKA inhibitor tested with dabrafenib and trametinib in BRAFV600E A375 melanoma cells and a 3D human melanoma skin model; combinations produced greater growth inhibition than single agents, with the triple regimen strongest, but no formal synergy metric was reported.

entities.name: Alisertib
observations: Selective AURKA inhibitor combined with trametinib in melanoma patient-derived xenografts; the combination showed strong ex vivo and in vivo tumor control, including BRAF-mutant and targeted-therapy-resistant models, without a reported formal synergy score.

entities.name: Dabrafenib
observations: Combined with MLN8054 in BRAFV600E A375 melanoma cells, producing greater antiproliferative effects than single agents.

entities.name: Trametinib
observations: Combined with MLN8054 in BRAFV600E A375 cells and with alisertib in melanoma PDX models; combinations enhanced antitumor effects and retained activity in resistant models.

entities.name: Melanoma
observations: Selective AURKA inhibition enhances BRAF/MEK pathway inhibitor activity in multiple preclinical melanoma models, but clinical benefit of these combinations remains unestablished.

entities.name: AURKA-MAPK enhancement
observations: In melanoma models, AURKA inhibition combined with BRAF or MEK inhibition increased antiproliferative, apoptotic, or tumor-control effects compared with single agents; formal pharmacologic synergy was not consistently demonstrated.

entities.name: Clinical evidence gap
observations: No direct clinical evidence was identified for combining selective AURKA inhibitors with approved melanoma BRAF or MEK inhibitors; clinical efficacy, safety, and translational feasibility remain unestablished.

entities.name: AURKA resistance vulnerability
observations: AURKA inhibition overcame or targeted compensatory MAPK resistance programs in BRAF- and NRAS-mutant melanoma models and showed activity in vemurafenib-resistant melanoma, although the latter was not a direct combination experiment.
